newsitem.title: USA: Witness recants Abu-Jamal testimony, is arrested.
newsitem.headline: Witness recants Abu-Jamal testimony, is arrested.

text.p: A former prostitute on Tuesday recanted her testimony in the 1982 murder trial of black activist Mumia Abu-Jamal and was arrested immediately after appearing in a Philadelphia court.
The woman, Veronica Jones, was placed under arrest by two Woodbury, New Jersey, police deputies on a 1992 arrest warrant for allegedly writing bad checks.
She had just completed testifying that she had been pressured by Philadelphia police to lie as a witness in Abu- Jamal's 1982 trial in the murder of a Philadelphia policeman.
"Don't drag me through the damn mud, I feel like I'm the one on trial now," a weeping Jones said as she was arrested.
Lawyers for Abu-Jamal, who are seeking to overturn his conviction and death sentence, called her arrest the latest example of official intimidation of witnesses.
Abu-Jamal's case attracted widespread attention among death-penalty opponents, foreign political leaders and Hollywood celebrities.
A one-time Black Panther and former radio journalist, he was convicted of killing policeman Daniel Faulkner in 1981 after a traffic stop.
Prosecutors said he was fairly convicted on eyewitness testimony and physical evidence, including spent bullets from his nearby gun.
But defence attorneys say that someone else killed the policeman and ran away and that Abu-Jamal's trial was marred by judicial bias and prosecutorial misconduct.
Jones told the court on Tuesday she had lied when testifying in 1982 that no one ran from the site of the killing.

In fact, she said, she had seen two people running and had told police about them. But she withheld that testimony after police said they would help her escape a long jail term on weapons charges, she said. "Right then and there, my kids was all I was thinking of," she explained.

Tuesday's hearing before Court of Common Pleas Judge Albert Sabo was held to consider whether Jones' testimony should be added to the appeal record. She had only recently been located after a long search by defence attorneys.
